description: Inspect a residential rough-in and its exterior feeders for wiring method violations: cable protection, support, burial depth, box fill and overhead clearances.
environmentDescription: A partly framed house with cables and boxes visible in the studs and joists, a trench to a detached garage, and an overhead feeder crossing the driveway.

violations.description: Cable runs through a bored hole 3/4 inch from the edge of a stud with no protective plate

citations.text: Cables and raceways through bored holes in wood framing need to sit at least 1-1/4 in from the nearest edge of the framing member; closer than that, a steel plate or sleeve at least 1/16 in thick must protect them.

violations.hintText: Check how far the hole is from the edge of the stud and whether a steel plate covers the cable.
violations.inspectionNote: The cable passes through a hole 3/4 in from the stud edge with no steel plate, so a nail or screw could reach it.

violations.description: NM cable runs 6 feet along a joist with no staples or straps

citations.text: Secure NM cable within 12 in of each box and fitting, and at least every 4-1/2 ft between those points.

violations.hintText: Look at how the cable is held along the joist. Count the supports between the boxes.
violations.inspectionNote: The cable hangs free for about 6 ft between boxes. It needs support at least every 4-1/2 ft and within 12 in of each box.

violations.description: Direct-buried UF cable to the detached garage is only 10 inches deep

citations.text: Direct-buried cable needs the cover depth in Table 300.5, normally 24 in. Shallower depths are allowed only in listed cases, such as 12 in for GFCI-protected residential circuits.

violations.hintText: Measure the depth of the trench and check whether the cable is in conduit.
violations.inspectionNote: The UF cable is 10 in below grade with no conduit. Direct-buried cable needs 24 in of cover, or 12 in on a GFCI-protected residential circuit.

violations.description: Device box holds more conductors than its volume allows

citations.text: A box must be large enough for everything in it: count each conductor, two for each device yoke, one for all the clamps and one for all the equipment grounds together, and multiply by the volume allowance for the conductor size.

violations.hintText: Count the conductors, the switch and the clamps in the box, then compare with the volume marked in the box.
violations.inspectionNote: A 12.5 cubic inch box holds six 12 AWG conductors, a switch, clamps and the grounds: about 22.5 cubic inches of required volume.

violations.description: Feeder to the garage crosses a residential driveway 9 feet above grade

citations.text: Overhead conductors of 300 V or less to ground need 12 ft of clearance over residential driveways; 10 ft is enough only where only pedestrians can reach them, and 18 ft is needed over public roads.

violations.hintText: Check how high the conductors are above the driveway where a vehicle passes.
violations.inspectionNote: The feeder is about 9 ft above the driveway. A residential driveway needs 12 ft of clearance.

violations.description: Type NM cable is folded around a sharp corner with an inside bend radius of only 1 inch

citations.text: Bends in this cable must not damage it. The inside edge of any bend, during or after installation, needs a radius of at least five times the cable diameter (major diameter for flat cable).

limit.quantity: inside bend radius of NM cable (cable major diameter 0.5 in.)

violations.hintText: Look at where the cable turns a corner. Does the curve look gentle or crimped?
violations.inspectionNote: The cable (about 0.5 in. across its wide side) makes a tight kink at a stud corner. Compare the inside radius of the curve with five times the cable width.

sceneFact.quantity: inside bend radius of NM cable (cable major diameter 0.5 in.)
sceneFact.note: radius of the inner edge of the bend, measured with a gauge at the kink

compliantFact.quantity: inside bend radius of NM cable (cable major diameter 0.5 in.)
compliantFact.note: radius of the inner edge of the bend

violations.description: Conductors at a small switch box stick out only 1 inch past the opening, too short to connect a device

citations.text: At each outlet, junction or switch point, leave at least 6 in. of free conductor for splices or device connections. If the opening is under 8 in. in any dimension, each conductor must reach at least 3 in. outside it.

limit.quantity: conductor length extending outside the box opening

violations.hintText: Check how much wire is left to work with at the open box.
violations.inspectionNote: At the rough-in switch box the cable ends are trimmed almost flush with the box mouth. Measure how far each conductor extends beyond the opening.

sceneFact.quantity: conductor length extending outside the box opening
sceneFact.note: measured from the box front edge to the conductor tips, opening smaller than 8 in.

compliantFact.quantity: conductor length extending outside the box opening
compliantFact.note: measured from the box front edge to the conductor tips

violations.description: NM cable comes up through the floor with only a 2 inch sleeve above the floor and no protection above that

citations.text: Where NM cable is subject to physical damage it must be protected by metal conduit, EMT, Schedule 80 PVC or another approved means. Where it passes through a floor, that enclosure must extend at least 6 in. above the floor.

limit.quantity: height of protective enclosure above floor

violations.hintText: Look at where a cable rises out of the floor. How high does its protection go?
violations.inspectionNote: A cable emerges from the floor at the wall base, shielded only by a short plastic stub. Measure the height of the protective sleeve above the floor.

sceneFact.quantity: height of protective enclosure above floor
sceneFact.note: measured from finished floor to the top of the sleeve

compliantFact.quantity: height of protective enclosure above floor
compliantFact.note: measured from finished floor to the top of the sleeve

violations.description: EMT run leaves a junction box with its first strap 6 feet away

citations.text: Tubing must be fastened within 3 ft of each box, cabinet, conduit body or other termination, and supported at intervals of no more than 10 ft. Up to 5 ft is allowed only where framing prevents 3 ft.

limit.quantity: distance from box to first EMT fastening

violations.hintText: Check how far the conduit travels from the box before it is first strapped.
violations.inspectionNote: A length of EMT enters a junction box on an open wall with no strap near the box. Measure from the box to the nearest strap or support.

sceneFact.quantity: distance from box to first EMT fastening
sceneFact.note: measured along the tubing from the box connector to the nearest strap, open wall with studs available

compliantFact.quantity: distance from box to first EMT fastening
compliantFact.note: measured along the tubing from the box connector to the nearest strap

violations.description: A 100 ft straight run of PVC conduit between two fixed boxes has no expansion fitting

citations.text: In a straight PVC run between securely mounted points such as boxes or elbows, an expansion fitting is needed when the expected length change from temperature is 1/4 in. or more, using the code table.

limit.quantity: expected thermal length change of straight PVC run with no expansion fitting

violations.hintText: Think about what heat does to plastic conduit that is fixed at both ends.
violations.inspectionNote: A long straight PVC conduit is rigidly strapped between two boxes on the outside wall with no sliding joint anywhere. With a 70 degree F swing, the table gives about 2.84 in. of movement per 100 ft.

sceneFact.quantity: expected thermal length change of straight PVC run with no expansion fitting
sceneFact.note: 100 ft run, 70 deg F temperature change, from the expansion table

compliantFact.quantity: expected thermal length change of straight PVC run with no expansion fitting
compliantFact.note: 5 ft run, 70 deg F temperature change: 2.84 in. per 100 ft x 5/100, or any run fitted with an expansion joint

violations.description: Device box sits 1/2 inch behind the finished drywall surface

citations.text: In gypsum or other noncombustible finishes, the front edge of a flush box or ring must not sit more than 1/4 in. behind the surface. In wood or other combustible finishes it must be flush or project.

limit.quantity: box front edge set back behind finished drywall surface

violations.hintText: Look at how a box sits relative to the wall surface once the board is up.
violations.inspectionNote: After drywall, the receptacle box front is recessed well into the wall cavity. Measure the gap between the box front edge and the wall face.

sceneFact.quantity: box front edge set back behind finished drywall surface
sceneFact.note: measured from the wall face to the front edge of the box, noncombustible drywall

compliantFact.quantity: box front edge set back behind finished drywall surface
compliantFact.note: measured from the wall face to the front edge of the box

violations.description: A junction box holding cable splices is buried behind finished drywall with no access opening

citations.text: Boxes and conduit bodies in buildings have to be installed so the wiring and devices inside are accessible. Accessible means reachable without damaging the building structure or finish and not permanently closed in by it.

violations.hintText: Splices have to be reachable later. Look for a box you could not open without damage to the wall.
violations.inspectionNote: A cable splice box sits between studs and is covered by painted drywall, with no cover plate or access panel in view. Opening it would mean cutting the wall.
